key_insight: Thermal history, alongside composition, controls hidden nanoscale octahedral-tilt order in lead halide perovskites, which in turn changes their optoelectronic response.
engineering_relevance: Processing ramps and thermal cycling should be treated as a design variable in perovskite device fabrication because they can shift local structure, phase behavior, and photoluminescence efficiency within operating conditions.
method: Single-crystal X-ray and neutron diffuse scattering across Cs/MA/FA and Cl/Br/I compositions
Machine-learning-assisted molecular dynamics plus a phenomenological octahedral tilt model
Hyperspectral photoluminescence to link local structure with optoelectronic response
evidence_signal: The study maps nearly every composition across accessible phases and reports equilibrium local nanodomains of correlated octahedral tilts, with heating-rate-dependent phase outcomes and PLQE changes in MAPbI3.
watch_item: The strong dependence on thermal ramp rate means processing history must be tightly controlled and reported, or device behavior may vary even for nominally identical compositions.
paper_title: Thermal history controls the optoelectronic response of lead halide perovskites through structure and dynamics
